notes:
Summary notes (shorthand):
- Use-case: product in-app help + knowledge search + intelligent rerank for personalization.
- Trial: 2-week Hosted API, ingested ~1.2M tokens (mix below). Team liked SDK, streaming.
- Observed metrics (hosted trial): p50 generation latency ~90ms (64-token outputs), p95 ~280ms, average token length 78. Total QPS observed during test bursts: sustained 18 QPS, peak 62 QPS (spikes from background sync jobs).
- Token mix captured for sizing: ~60% short responses (10-60 tokens), ~25% medium (61-200 tokens), ~15% long (200-800 tokens). Typical request: prompt 150 tokens, expected generation 40-120 tokens depending on flow.
- Concurrency: app-level concurrency typically 8 active user streams, expected to scale to 30 during product launches.
- Desired SLOs: p95 < 200ms for short responses; p95 < 600ms for long completions. Latency sensitivity is high for chat flows.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market procurement. They prefer committed monthly reserved capacity with burstable headroom. Target ARR bucket 75k-200k.
- Model preferences: open-models tuned for instruction following. Want ability to pin model versions and automatic fallbacks to cheaper quantized variants for non-critical paths.
- Dedicated ask: Redwood proposed 2x H100 (80GB) nodes for baseline, 4x H100 with autoscale/burst for peak – Elmshore requested the math behind throughput assumptions.
- POC requests: 1) run production-like traffic replay for 48h on Dedicated test pool, 2) end-to-end cost per 1M tokens calc with and without KV caching + batching, 3) routing test: latency-first vs cost-first policy.
- Security: must have SSO + audit logs to meet customer compliance; data residency option for EU customers later.
- Quote from CTO (call 2026-01-05): "We can tolerate a bit more cost up-front if latency is predictable. Want dedicated capacity for launches — but need numbers we can justify to finance."
- Next steps (short): entregate Dedicated sizing doc, provide 48h replay window, get security sign-off artifacts to Elmshore security team.
